summary: C-J1 (FS-GG/.github#4710) binds the Coordination managed-group owner, pinned at (FS-GG/FS.GG.Coordination, ac22206560f3eddfea524ce8f752ff1d0dfeec4e, eng/managed_group_owner.py, sha256 d846dbe1..., 45315 bytes), into the inline caller of the fable-reference-public.yml job wasm-installed-c. The caller fetches the owner through its closed acquisition path, checks size and SHA-256 before import, then checks the contract and the owner's self-hash. It probes containment before provisioning and qualifies actual tool versions under the setup deadline. Every call is one require-empty run under one never-renewed phase deadline, with a fresh out_dir under the job root. Executables are identity-bound with a recorded basis, and the hashes of declared script inputs (validator, checker) are retained per group. The job's Python runs in a sudo systemd-run delegated unit with TasksMax/MemoryMax hard limits. Installed C is wired per invocation. The shell checker's --mode wasm prepares only the downloaded source and production graph and runs no browser. The caller's installed_c runs that checker as one group, then each family's Playwright --list and test invocation as its own group, and applies the 9-case list and result assertions per family. The browser host validator is content-addressed, so its hash is in the profile argv. Lessons: the supplier refuses control characters in argv; a test should validate every real call site against the real validate_profile at run time; cwd must lie inside the profile root; and a nested owner inside a leaf cannot work (the root would not be exclusive), so Playwright must be launched from the top-level owner. The WASM receiver targets published Workspace.Template 0.19.2 (archive ef5c5c2f..., source and peeled tag d15f085f, descriptor e8dbf895...), verified locally by publication check, signatures, scaffolds and receiver check. Correction (run 39858275028): that local verification did not run the caller's ProviderTool restore argv. That argv passed -p:DisableImplicitLibraryPacksFolder=true, which fails NU1403 against the lock's SDK library-pack FSharp.Core (record templates/wasm-installed-c-run-39858275028). provider_tool_restore_argv now omits the flag, while generated-product restores in the checker keep it. The SDK acquisition, closed NuGet config and Fable/ProviderTool argv are named caller functions, and the always-run installed-c-restore-control.yml executes them, plus the checker's verbatim generation and restore lines, from clean caches on every PR and main push. Still held: both steps (if: false), main() (RUNTIME_ADMITTED=False) and custody_gate before installed C; installed-c.json records failed with its first cause. The custody pilot (runs 39828121993, 39837319401 and 39845591542; record templates/wasm-custody-pilot-run-39845591542) has since established, on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (WebKit with recorded host packages) clean stock shutdown under require-empty, deadline retirement, owner survivor retirement and the Chromium support join; its pilot entry is now closed (PILOT_ADMISSION=None). Installed C has a held, separately admitted dispatch entry: .github/workflows/wasm-installed-c.yml job installed-c, whose first step refuses before any host write unless source carries the admission, and admitted_installed_sequence. While the literal INSTALLED_ADMISSION = None, that entry refuses before any acquisition. Once an admission PR sets it to the exact comment URL, the entry runs in order: validate the dispatch (main, admitted_ref = SHA = WORKFLOW_SHA = head, exact URL, attempt 1, unit, host evidence); load the owner and probe; require the unit read-back to match (TasksMax=6144, MemoryMax=12G, RuntimeMaxUSec=40min); require the recorded WebKit packages to be installed with no apt or dpkg process left (the step is byte-identical to the pilot's); run prepare_inputs and qualify_tools; open custody_gate(admitted=True) for itself only; run installed_c (27 cases) under INSTALLED_BUDGET (setup 840 s, installed 1230 s); collect evidence capped at 150 MiB. hosted_sequence, main() (RUNTIME_ADMITTED=False) and both literal-false steps stay closed and are not the lift path. One run is enforced by the admission plan (dispatch once, then a reset PR sets the constant back to None). The first admitted run (39858275028) spent its admission and failed as evidence at that restore. A local rehearsal of the fixed source passed 27/27 with the owner launch substituted. Recording added before run 2 (#744; recording only, no custody change): every managed receipt carries highWater via the owner's public run(control=) hook, which is read-only and never raises. Group scope is the leaf's pids.peak and pids.events max; leaf memory is null by design, because only the pids controller is enabled there. Unit scope is the cumulative pids.peak and memory.peak, per-group oom/max event deltas, sampled memory.current, and memory.current/anon at birth and removal with deltas from the previous group. installed-run.json records the phase wall-clock (setup, installed, checker, per-family list/test, sequence) against INSTALLED_BUDGET. The checker's two GETs are bounded with --retry 3 --retry-all-errors and its git ls-remote with 3 bounded attempts; bytes are still hash-checked. Run 2 (39874053570; record templates/wasm-installed-c-run-39874053570) established hosted: every setup step, qualify_tools, the checker source stage and Chromium's 9 cases, with all 25 groups that ran contained under the real owner (groups 7-25 for the first time) and measured budgets and peaks far below the limits. It failed at Firefox case 1 on the product's 250 ms EndToEndFromEnqueue policy deadline, which spans cold module-Worker boot (FS-GG/FS.GG.Game#727). Not established hosted: Firefox and WebKit runtime passes and the full 27-case journey; provenance of installer-output and host images; CPU pressure; plus the pilot's recorded gaps (liveness at the deadline, per-browser argv, one WebKit build and package set, an orphaned browser).
title: Installed-WASM caller binds fsgg.managed-group-contract/1 and holds a separately admitted 0.19.2 dispatch entry
